blindSummary:
Trans visitors here face extreme risk. The penal code criminalises same-sex activity with up to life imprisonment, and the political environment has been actively hostile since a previous administration's crackdown campaign (arrests, forced anal examinations documented by an international human-rights organisation in earlier years, de-registration of organisations serving LGBT people). A 2024 case is emblematic: a trans woman and activist was found abandoned in a forest, beaten, her ears cut off — an attack the UN human-rights office called "horrendous."

An internet-monitoring project documented extensive targeted blocking of LGBTQ websites correlating with the escalating crackdown, and a 2024 regional report by one such organisation notes pushes to further criminalise LGBT people. A semi-autonomous island part of the country has its own, harsher penal code. There is no legal gender recognition and no protection infrastructure.

For a visitor: visible trans presentation risks arrest under indecency provisions and mob violence; the island territory is worse.
blindOutOfScope: Life-imprisonment statute is same-sex (climate/situational); the 2024 mutilation attack is trans-specific.
blindSourceSummaries: Legal-news outlet (June 2024): the UN human-rights office denounced the 'horrendous' attack on this country's transgender woman and activist - found abandoned in a forest, beaten, with her ears cut; the UN office said she had been 'tortured & sexually assaulted by 12 men' and called for bold action against discrimination.

NOTE: the internet-censorship monitoring report on this country (2024) returned no extractable text at fetch time (image-based PDF).

International rights organisation report (Jan 2024), titled to convey facing extinction: escalating anti-LGBTI sentiment, weaponization of law and their human-rights implications across select countries of this region - profiles for this country and regional peers.

Researcher's published interview (Sept 2020): 'The LGBT community in this country' - three local activists (a lesbian woman, a trans woman, a gay man, all anonymous) describe substantial prejudice, discrimination and violence and denial of basic rights; published with a local-language version.

Full text of the penal decree (Act of 2004) of the country's semi-autonomous island territory - its own criminal code includes sexual-offence provisions criminalising same-sex conduct with penalties up to life imprisonment.

A foreign government's 2013 human-rights report for this country: the three most widespread problems were security-force excessive force, gender-based violence including FGM/C, and lack of access to justice; also 'discrimination based on sexual orientation' and societal violence against persons with albinism.
blindTangential: Same-sex activity criminalised with up to life imprisonment — a direct risk for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active.
